target.title: feat: render responsive Markdown tables
target.body:
## Summary

- render Markdown tables inside a dedicated horizontal-scroll wrapper
- preserve native table layout and GFM column alignment
- keep wide tables contained within the message surface on narrow screens
- expose overflowing tables as named, keyboard-focusable regions
- regenerate the checked-in embedded webassets

## Why

Wide Markdown tables could overflow the message layout. Applying scrolling directly to the table also changes it from native table layout, which can break grid sizing. The wrapper provides overflow containment while the table remains `display: table`.

## Real behavior proof

Verified inside the actual authenticated ClickClack app at a 480 x 720 viewport. The proof flow opened `/app`, loaded the bootstrapped `#general` channel, sent a wide aligned Markdown table through the real message composer, located the resulting non-pending message row, and horizontally scrolled that row's table.

| Observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Page identity | title `ClickClack`, heading `#general`, routed channel URL |
| Message path | sent through the real `Message body` composer and `Send` button |
| Rendered surface | visible `.message-row:not(.is-pending)` inside the ClickClack timeline |
| Scroll wrapper width | `clientWidth = 404px` |
| Wide content width | `scrollWidth = 671px` |
| Wrapper overflow | `overflow-x: auto` |
| Accessible region | `role="region"`, `aria-label="Scrollable Markdown table"`, `tabindex="0"` |
| Table layout | `display: table`, width `671.453px` |
| GFM column alignment | left / center / right preserved |
| Horizontal interaction | `scrollLeft: 0 -> 260` |
| Keyboard interaction | focus region, press `ArrowRight`, observe `scrollLeft > 0` |
| Framework overlay | none |
| Browser console | 0 warnings, 0 errors |

Before horizontal scroll, inside ClickClack:

![ClickClack general channel showing a wide Markdown table contained in a real message row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/codex/markdown-tables-pr/docs/review-proof/clickclack-markdown-table-before.png)

After horizontal scroll, inside ClickClack:

![ClickClack general channel showing the same message table scrolled to its centered and right-aligned columns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/codex/markdown-tables-pr/docs/review-proof/clickclack-markdown-table-after.png)

## Validation

- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm exec playwright test` - 99 passed
- focused real-app test: `CLICKCLACK_E2E_PORT=18194 pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/markdown-table.spec.ts` - 1 passed
- repeatability gate: `git diff --exit-code -- apps/api/internal/webassets/dist`
- Autoreview: clean, no actionable findings, `patch is correct` (0.97)
- ClawSweeper final exact-head pass: no findings, security cleared, proof sufficient (Tier A), `patch is correct` (0.94)

target.title: feat: support split frontend and API origins
target.body:
## Summary

- add `CLICKCLACK_PUBLIC_API_URL` as a strictly validated canonical API base while keeping `CLICKCLACK_PUBLIC_URL` as the frontend/browser origin
- preserve same-origin behavior by default; when the API URL is omitted it resolves to the frontend origin
- inject the API base into the built frontend and route API, realtime, upload, avatar, artifact, OAuth, and setup-code traffic through it
- allow credentialed browser access only from the exact configured frontend origin, with bounded preflights, consistent `Vary` headers, CSRF enforcement, and secure cookie policy
- add version 1 setup-code metadata: exact `claim_url` and canonical `api_base_url` on mint, plus the canonical API base on claim
- document split-origin and path-mounted deployment requirements; update OpenAPI, generated SDK types, tests, and Unreleased changelog

## Configuration and trust policy

`CLICKCLACK_PUBLIC_API_URL` accepts a canonical origin plus an optional normalized base path. Remote deployments require HTTPS. Loopback split deployments may use HTTP only when both frontend and API use the same loopback hostname. Credentials, query strings, fragments, dot segments, duplicate separators, encoded path separators, whitespace, backslashes, and unsupported path characters fail startup validation.

Browser CORS is exact-origin and credentialed. Session/OAuth cookies remain `HttpOnly` and `Secure` where required, use `SameSite=Lax` for same-site origins and `SameSite=None` for cross-site HTTPS origins, and are scoped to the configured API base path. Path-mounted namespaced HTTPS cookies use `__Secure-`; origin-root cookies retain `__Host-`.

## OpenClaw coordination (consumer repo; not changed here)

OpenClaw needs a follow-up consumer change before split-origin setup URIs can be claimed:

1. Continue accepting the legacy `https://server/#CODE` form and append `/api/bot-setup-codes/claim` only for that origin-root form.
2. Recognize a pre-fragment URL ending in `/api/bot-setup-codes/claim` as the exact version 1 claim endpoint and POST `{ "code": "..." }` to it unchanged, including any API base path.
3. Validate setup URLs before network access: HTTPS for remote hosts; HTTP only for loopback; no URL credentials or query; fragment contains only the setup code; reject redirects (or at minimum any redirect changing the canonical origin/path). Do not attach an existing bot/session credential to the claim request.
4. Require `contract_version: 1` for the new response shape. Canonicalize and validate `api_base_url`, and require the exact claim URL to equal `api_base_url + "/api/bot-setup-codes/claim"` before persisting it.
5. Persist the returned `api_base_url` exactly, including its base path, as the ClickClack account `baseUrl`; use it for REST and realtime traffic. Retain the current legacy response fallback when version/base fields are absent.
6. Add consumer tests for legacy same-origin, split hostname, path-mounted API, malformed endpoints, redirect/mismatch rejection, single-use claim failure, and atomic config/hot-reload behavior.

## Proof

- `pnpm check` — passed: all Go tests; web/SDK builds and typechecks; FakeCo AWS 30/30; desktop 13/13; lint and formatting
- `pnpm coverage` — passed: 85.4% filtered request/business-logic coverage (85% required)
- `pnpm test:e2e` — passed: 98/98
- focused Go origin/config/API tests — passed
- AutoReview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings

Live split-origin deployment used the real built server with the frontend proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:18190` and API on `http://127.0.0.1:18191`:

- frontend returned 200, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and injected API base `http://127.0.0.1:18191`
- trusted credentialed preflight returned 204 with the exact frontend origin; an untrusted origin returned 403 without an allow-origin header
- cross-origin magic-link consume returned 200, set the namespaced `HttpOnly` session cookie, and authenticated `/api/me` returned 200
- realtime WebSocket connected with the frontend `Origin`; a new message returned 201 and the socket received the matching `message.created` event ID
- setup mint returned 201 with contract version 1 and the exact API claim URL; unauthenticated claim returned 200 with contract version 1 and the canonical API base

Fixes #90
